task_instance: Created a sample refs.bib with 5 entries containing two duplicate pairs (one matched by identical DOI, one matched by same normalized title+year) plus one unique entry with inconsistent title capitalization. Wrote clean_bib.py using bibtexparser to: parse refs.bib, merge duplicate entries keeping the most complete one (union of fields), regenerate citation keys as lastnameYEARfirstword, protect capitalized non-first words in titles with braces, and write refs_clean.bib plus a changes.md report describing every merge/rename/protection decision.
evidence: Installed bibtexparser 2.0.1 via `pip install bibtexparser`. Ran `python3 clean_bib.py` which parsed refs.bib (5 entries), merged the DOI-duplicate pair (smith2020a/smith2020dup -> smith2020deep) and the title+year-duplicate pair (doe2019/doe2019b -> doe2019graph) keeping the more complete entry in each case, regenerated all 3 resulting keys as lastnameYEARfirstword (smith2020deep, doe2019graph, turing1950computing), and brace-protected capitalized title words (e.g. 'Deep Learning for Natural Language Processing' -> 'Deep {Learning} for {Natural} {Language} {Processing}'). Verified refs_clean.bib re-parses correctly with bibtexparser (3 entries, 0 failed_blocks). Output files: refs_clean.bib and changes.md in the work directory, alongside the source refs.bib and clean_bib.py script.
